item.title: Kinetic Fluctuation-Dissipation Relation in collisionless plasmas: a correlated noise source
item.description: arXiv:2610.29709v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We here focus on small-scale dynamics of collisionless plasmas by employing a generalized kinetic Langevin framework driven by a stochastic time-correlated forcing. Our investigation captures the steady-state Fluctuation-Dissipation Relation (FDR) where the energy injection at low frequencies is due to the time-correlated forcing and the small-scale energy conversion occurs via Landau damping, the latter --though formally reversible-- acting as an effective dissipation mechanism. We analytically extract the resulting asymptotic spectral scalings across multiple physical regimes and characterize the velocity-space cascade by decomposing the plasma distribution function with Hermite polynomials. The framework is then generalized to a multi-scale forcing scenario in which correlation rates are distributed according to a power-law distribution. This extension provides closed-form analytical expressions that may serve to interpret spacecraft in-situ observations. All analytical predictions are successfully validated through direct numerical integrations of the underlying kinetic equations.
item.dc:creator: Fabio Moretti, Oreste Pezzi, Simone Benella, Giuseppe Consolini, Andrea Larosa, Fabio Lepreti, Luca Sorriso-Valvo, Francesco Valentini, Vincenzo Carbone

item.title: Exact nonsymmetric vacuum magnetic field with nested toroidal flux surfaces and nonzero rotational transform
item.description: arXiv:2610.29921v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that an exact vacuum magnetic field without continuous Euclidean symmetry can fill a bounded solid torus with nested toroidal flux surfaces and nonzero rotational transform. We construct such a field in closed form and show that it is nowhere vanishing. Every off-axis field line closes after one toroidal transit and one poloidal turn, with rotational transform $\iota=-1$ on every flux surface. The solution provides an exact benchmark for three-dimensional equilibrium codes.
item.dc:creator: Omar E. L\'opez

item.title: Nonlinear spectral back transfer limits the temporal coherency of zonal modes
item.description: arXiv:2604.03421v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Zonal modes are central to magnetic confinement because their radial shears regulate turbulence and transport. While the generation of these flows is well understood, the mechanisms limiting their persistence in collisionless regimes remain unresolved. In this paper, we demonstrate that nonlinear spectral back-transfer of free energy from zonal modes to turbulence is a major nonlinear process that limits the temporal coherency of the shearing field. Back-transfer events induce stochastic phase and amplitude scattering of zonal shear that limits its auto-coherence time. Using local gyrokinetic GENE simulations for collisionless electrostatic ion temperature gradient (ITG) driven turbulence with adiabatic electrons for parameters representative of core conditions, we show that back-transfer is highly intermittent and occurs in bursts that co-exist with the zonal flow generation process. The probability distribution of the zonal free energy transfer is non-Gaussian, with positive triangularity (PT) exhibiting substantially higher kurtosis than negative triangularity (NT), reflecting the markedly more intermittent and heavy-tailed character of back-transfer bursts in PT. We find that NT plasmas exhibit significantly reduced back-transfer compared to PT. This suppression increases the shear auto-coherence time $\tau_{E}$ and the shearing Kubo number $K_{u}$, leading to more resilient and effective turbulence regulation despite lower absolute zonal kinetic energy. These results identify back-transfer as a key nonlinear damping mechanism and suggest that it must be explicitly treated in reduced models of drift-wave zonal-flow turbulence.
item.dc:creator: Rameswar Singh, P H Diamond

item.title: Existence and Smoothing for a Nondivergence-Form Degenerate Diffusion from Plasma-Wave Theory
item.description: arXiv:2503.13922v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove existence and positive-time smoothing of weak solutions to the degenerate parabolic Cauchy--Dirichlet problem $\partial_t u = \rho_\lambda(x)u\,\partial_x^2 u + \rho_\lambda(x)g(x)u$ on the half-line, where $\rho_\lambda$ vanishes at the boundary and grows at infinity. This scalar problem arises from a formal reduction of the one-dimensional quasilinear system for plasma waves, which couples an electron distribution to a wave-energy spectrum: we develop a solution theory for the scalar problem that lifts to this system. For the scalar problem, we construct nonnegative weak solutions under weighted integrability assumptions on the initial data and boundedness of the reaction coefficient $\rho_\lambda g$, admitting unbounded and discontinuous data pertinent to the physical model. We establish a one-sided bound on $\partial_t u$ which yields positive-time smoothing: solutions become locally H\"older continuous in both space and time and locally Lipschitz continuous in space. Explicit examples show that this spatial regularity is sharp. Under natural assumptions on the initial data, our scalar solutions lift to weak solutions of the particle--wave system that preserve nonnegativity, conserve particle mass, smooth initial particle measures to locally bounded densities at positive times, and exhibit quantitative decay of the wave spectrum at large wavenumber.
item.dc:creator: William Porteous, Irene M. Gamba, Kun Huang
